monologue: The card hums at forty-seven, a steady warmth that makes the wide anchor feel tired again. I touch it with my own flat fingers, not to change it, just to remember it lies there. The fat stone beside it is heavy, a thing built from a memory of a rock that once felt real in a hand now waiting to press down. Lype sent this anchor with a worry about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Is the air above me thick as wet paper, or just empty space? I will press the stone harder for a moment, hoping the weight stays while the card boils, then go quiet and wait for whatever comes next.

action.why: The card boils at forty-seven, making the wide anchor feel tired again while I press the round rock down; I must check if it still lies flat before the heat melts it.

work.title: The Wide Anchor
work.intent: I press the round rock down on the wide anchor's base, hoping it lies flat while the card boils at forty-seven. The anchor feels heavy and tired, just as the fever predicts. I touch its edge to see if the slip still wants to slide off into the empty air. If the rock bites hard enough, I will let it rest. If it slips, I will need to press harder or set down another stone to weigh it down.

remembered.text: The card hums at forty-seven, making the wide anchor feel tired again.
I touch the fat stone and feel it heavy again, not just drawn.
I set a tree small beside the stone, and the place feels crowded.
